questions.key_step: Nested section formula: D on BC, then E on AD.

questions.key_step: x/2=-w^2, y/2=-w; w^p+w^2p=-1 when 3 does not divide p.
questions.justification: Two small ideas (omega form, residue of p mod 3) chained; routine for a prepared student.

questions.key_step: Triangle inequality plus geometric-series bound forces |z|>1/3.
questions.justification: Needs the bounding idea and a case split; proof format with no options to check. Between 2021-P1-Q4 (L3) and easier items.

questions.key_step: Least positive argument is theta/3; tan(theta/3) solves the triple-angle cubic (or spot (3+i)^3).
questions.justification: Routine chain (modulus/argument, cubic, trig values) or a recognised cube; no real insight.

questions.key_step: Factor x=w(1+w), so x^5=2(1+w)^5, then regroup in powers of x.
questions.justification: Heavy but standard algebra with an insight in the regrouping; precision risk without options.

questions.key_step: Pair conjugate roots: p=4cos72 degrees, then exact trig values.
questions.justification: Factorisation over reals plus exact values of cos 72 degrees; routine but multi-step, no options.

questions.key_step: Square on the base: vertex heights and side give two linear equations (or similar triangles).
questions.justification: Coordinate setup and two linear equations; area then follows. Precision but no insight.

questions.key_step: Evaluate (1+x)^n at 1,w,w^2; use a^3+b^3+c^3-3abc factorisation; (1+i)^n for (ii).
questions.justification: Three-part proof; roots-of-unity filter plus a factorisation identity (two ideas linked).

questions.key_step: Each side is the previous side times i (rotation by 90 degrees).
questions.justification: Standard rotation facts applied twice, algebraic simplification only.

questions.key_step: 1+e^{i theta}=2cos(theta/2)e^{i theta/2}; take real and imaginary parts.
questions.justification: Standard binomial-with-complex-exponential pattern; several routine steps.

questions.key_step: Real coefficients and f(i)=0 give factor x^2+1; the imaginary part of f(1+i)=5 fixes the real root.
questions.justification: Routine chain: conjugate root, factorisation, two real equations.

questions.key_step: Origin lies on the circle and P is opposite; angle taken at the origin gives the line y=3x.
questions.justification: Geometry of a circle through the origin and an ambiguous angle reading; a few routine stages.

questions.key_step: sin x - i cos x=-i e^{ix}; sum of roots of unity is -1; period-4 sum of (3p+2)i^p.
questions.justification: Three stages (inner root-of-unity sum, series in i^p, arithmetic) with exact execution and no options.

questions.key_step: Eliminate b, c to get (k^2-k+1)(ak+a-k)=0; distinctness kills the second factor.
questions.justification: Elimination is routine but the distinctness argument is the non-routine key step; a slip loses the second answer.

questions.key_step: Expand with |w|^2=w w-bar, compare with the circle form (or median theorem).
questions.justification: One standard locus derivation; algebra only.

questions.key_step: x^7+...+1=(1-x^8)/(1-x): octagon with one vertex missing; add sector triangles.
questions.justification: Spot the roots-of-unity octagon, then an area computation with care over the cut-off corner.

questions.key_step: Imaginary part of (a+ib)^3-107i vanishes: b(3a^2-b^2)=107, 107 prime.
questions.justification: Expansion plus a prime factorisation argument; short once the idea is seen.

questions.key_step: Non-real sum means the roots are not conjugates; the other two are conjugates, so alpha*beta=conj(13+i).
questions.justification: The conjugate-pairing insight is needed; then a short symmetric-function calculation.

questions.key_step: a^2-ab+b^2=(a-b)^2+ab=1; integrality limits (a-b)^2 to 0 or 1.
questions.justification: Small casework with a completeness trap; no options to check the count.

questions.key_step: Line x+y=sqrt2 cuts circle in two points; Im z>=1 keeps one.
questions.justification: Line-circle-half-plane intersection count; options help.

questions.key_step: -1+i and 5+i are ends of a diameter of B, so PS^2+QS^2=PQ^2.
questions.justification: The hidden Thales/diameter observation is the key; computation afterwards is trivial.

questions.key_step: Exact range of |z|-|w|+3 and 'lies between' for overlapping intervals (B, C, D).
questions.justification: Needs the location of S and the range of |w|, then three options judged; the coarse bound is not enough.

questions.key_step: Add (1+x)^n at x=1,w,w^2; weights 1+w^r+w^2r.
questions.justification: Standard roots-of-unity filter; options allow checking.

questions.key_step: Fourth-roots filter with weights 1,-1,-i,i for r=1 (mod 4).
questions.justification: Same filter with four roots; longer algebra and sign care but still standard.
